Hi Dylan,

We're preparing our SIG and CAIQ for an impending audit and need additional detail on Redwood's supply chain controls related to privileged access and key management. Specifically, can you provide:

- A current list of subprocessors that have any form of privileged or administrative access to customer data (including maintenance/ops tools) and the scope of their access.
- Evidence of KMS/HSM usage and key custody for production models (keyflow diagram and attestation of HSM-backed keys if any).
- Sample audit logs for a 30-day window (anonymized) showing privileged access events.

We're targeting a deadline of May 18 for this package. Please let me know if that works and what artifacts you can deliver.

Thanks,
Anya

Hi Anya — following up with the technical detail Dylan mentioned. A couple of short answers up front then the artifacts we can provide:

Short answers:
- HSM / key custody: Our production platform uses an HSM-backed KMS (AWS CloudHSM for hosted deployments; for Dedicated we offer integration with customer KMS/HSM or a dedicated HSM cluster). Service-level keys used for model-serving are stored with HSM protection; customer-managed keys are supported via BYOK flows.
- Privileged/admin tooling: Third-party vendors with privileged tool access are limited to a small set of maintenance partners (listed in the CSV). Their access is time-bound, role-scoped, and logged to our SIEM.

Artifacts we can deliver by May 18 (or sooner):
- HSM attestation statement (text) — confirms HSM-backed key usage for platform service keys.
- KMS keyflow diagram (attached; already provided by Dylan) and an appendix documenting which keys are customer-controlled vs platform-controlled.
- Anonymized privileged-access log extract for a 30-day window (CSV) — we'll redact usernames/IDs and provide event types + timestamps + vendor identifier.

A few questions for you to help scope the redaction and filters so we don't accidentally expose customer identifiers:
1) Do you prefer event-level granularity (every sudo/priv action) or an aggregated view (counts by vendor/action)?
2) Is there a specific 30-day window you want us to use (we can provide rolling 30 days ending on any date you choose)?

We also maintain a Confluence page with our subprocessor onboarding and privileged-access controls; here's the link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/security/subprocessors/kms-keyflow

If you want a signed HSM attestation we can route that through our compliance team — would MedStream require a notarized statement or is an internal attestation sufficient for your SIG assessor?

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Staff Engineer, Infrastructure Security
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Dylan / Karthik — this is great, thank you. A couple of follow-ups from our assessor:

- Please include a second, narrower log extract that shows the three most recent elevated actions for each privileged vendor (event type, timestamp, vendor label). That helps the assessor validate rotation & access timing.
- We also need confirmation of encryption-at-rest for model artifacts and backups (certificate or short note is fine).
- Regarding attestations: the assessor prefers a signed HSM attestation (PDF) where possible.

If you can deliver the narrower log extract plus the signed attestation and the encryption confirmation by EOD May 18 that should close the highest-priority gaps. Once we have those we may follow up with a short set of SIG-lite question clarifications.
